description: This topic explains how to identify types and parts of photographs, estimate size and distance, recognise physical and human features, and understand the uses, limitations and comparison of photographs with maps.

mcq.questionText: Which type of photograph is taken with the camera held at a normal eye-level position on the ground?
mcq.explanation: A ground or horizontal photograph is taken from ground level, so the camera looks at objects roughly side-on at eye level.

mcq.questionText: A photograph taken from an aircraft with the camera pointing straight down at the ground is called a:
mcq.explanation: In a vertical aerial photograph the camera axis is pointed vertically downward, giving a plan-like view similar to a map.

mcq.questionText: Which part of a photograph is nearest to the camera and usually shows the largest, clearest details?
mcq.explanation: The foreground is the area closest to the camera, so its objects appear largest and in the most detail.

mcq.questionText: An oblique aerial photograph is taken when the camera is:

options.text: Held at ground level facing forward
In an aircraft pointing straight downward
In an aircraft tilted at an angle to the ground
Placed flat on the ground facing the sky

mcq.explanation: An oblique aerial photograph is taken from the air with the camera tilted at an angle, so it shows the sides and tops of features.

mcq.questionText: Which part of a photograph lies farthest from the camera and often includes the horizon?
mcq.explanation: The background is the most distant part of the photograph and usually contains the horizon and far-off features.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a HUMAN feature that may be seen on a photograph?
mcq.explanation: A tarmac road is made by people, so it is a human (cultural) feature, while rivers, mountains and forests are physical features.

mcq.questionText: Which type of photograph gives a view most similar to a map?
mcq.explanation: A vertical aerial photograph shows features from directly above, giving a plan view like a map.

mcq.questionText: On a ground photograph, the apparent size of an object depends mainly on:

options.text: The time the photo was taken

mcq.explanation: Objects nearer the camera appear larger and those far away appear smaller, so distance affects apparent size.

mcq.questionText: Which is a major LIMITATION of using photographs in geography?

options.text: They show real colours of features
They do not show place names or a scale
They record features at one moment

mcq.explanation: Unlike maps, photographs usually have no names, scale or grid, making exact measurement and naming difficult.

mcq.questionText: To estimate the height of a person standing in the foreground of a photograph, you can compare them with a known object such as a:

options.text: Door or window of a building near them

mcq.explanation: Comparing an object with a nearby item of known size, such as a door, helps estimate its size or distance.

mcq.questionText: Which statement BEST describes an advantage of photographs over written descriptions?

options.text: They explain the causes of features
They give a clear visual record of an area at a glance
They always include a scale bar

mcq.explanation: Photographs capture the actual appearance of an area quickly and clearly, which is hard to achieve with words alone.

mcq.questionText: In a vertical aerial photograph, features are usually identified by their:

options.text: Shape, size, tone and pattern from above

mcq.explanation: Because vertical photographs show a plan view, interpreters rely on shape, size, tone and pattern to recognise features.

mcq.questionText: When comparing a photograph with a map of the same area, a key difference is that the map:

options.text: Shows the true colours of vegetation
Uses symbols, a scale and a key
Shows people and moving vehicles clearly
Records the weather at that moment

mcq.explanation: A map represents features using agreed symbols, a fixed scale and a key, while a photograph shows actual appearance without symbols.

mcq.questionText: Why might distant features in the background of a photograph be hard to identify accurately?

options.text: They appear small, faint and may be hidden by haze
They are drawn using map symbols
They are always larger than foreground features

mcq.explanation: Background features are far away, so they look small and blurred and can be obscured by haze or poor visibility.

mcq.questionText: A study requires measuring the exact area of farm plots in a region. Which choice is MOST suitable and why?

options.text: An oblique aerial photograph, because it shows the sides of plots
A topographical map, because it has a scale for accurate measurement
A ground photograph, because it shows the nearest plot clearly
A background view, because distant plots look smaller

mcq.explanation: A map has a known scale and plan view, allowing accurate area measurement, which photographs without scale cannot easily provide.

fib.questionText: A photograph taken from ground level at eye height is called a ground or _____ photograph.
fib.explanation: Ground photographs are also known as horizontal photographs because the camera looks across the landscape.

fib.questionText: A photograph taken from an aircraft with the camera pointing straight down is a _____ aerial photograph.
fib.explanation: Vertical aerial photographs give a plan view of the ground, similar to a map.

fib.questionText: A photograph taken from the air with the camera tilted at an angle is an _____ aerial photograph.
fib.explanation: Oblique aerial photographs show both the tops and sides of features.

fib.questionText: The part of a photograph closest to the camera is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The foreground contains the nearest objects, which appear largest and clearest.

fib.questionText: The part of a photograph that lies between the nearest and farthest areas is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The middleground is found between the foreground and the background.

fib.questionText: The most distant part of a photograph, often containing the horizon, is the _____.
fib.explanation: The background shows far-off features, which appear small and faint.

fib.questionText: Features such as rivers, hills and forests that are made by nature are called _____ features.
fib.explanation: Physical (natural) features are not created by people, unlike human-made features.

fib.questionText: Features such as roads, houses and bridges that are made by people are called _____ features.
fib.explanation: Human (cultural) features are constructed by people, such as buildings and roads.

fib.questionText: To estimate the size of an object in a photograph, it is compared with another object of _____ size.
fib.explanation: Comparing an unknown object with one of known size helps estimate its real size or distance.

fib.questionText: Unlike a map, a photograph usually lacks a _____, which makes exact distance measurement difficult.
fib.explanation: Maps have a scale for accurate measurement, while ordinary photographs do not.

tf.questionText: A vertical aerial photograph is taken from an aircraft with the camera pointing straight downward.
tf.explanation: In a vertical aerial photograph the camera axis points vertically down, giving a plan view.

tf.questionText: A ground photograph is taken from high above the earth using an aircraft.
tf.explanation: A ground photograph is taken from ground level, not from an aircraft; aerial photographs are taken from the air.

tf.questionText: Objects in the foreground of a photograph appear larger than similar objects in the background.
tf.explanation: Because the foreground is closer to the camera, its objects look larger than distant ones.

tf.questionText: An oblique aerial photograph shows only the tops of features and never their sides.
tf.explanation: An oblique photograph is taken at an angle, so it shows both the tops and the sides of features.

tf.questionText: A river is an example of a human-made feature on a photograph.
tf.explanation: A river is a physical (natural) feature; human features include roads and buildings.

tf.questionText: A vertical aerial photograph gives a view that is more similar to a map than a ground photograph does.
tf.explanation: Both vertical photographs and maps show features from directly above in plan view.

tf.questionText: Photographs always show place names and a scale just like maps.
tf.explanation: Ordinary photographs lack names, scale and a key, which is one of their limitations.

tf.questionText: Comparing an object with a known item such as a doorway helps to estimate its real size in a photograph.
tf.explanation: Using a familiar object of known size as a guide allows reasonable size estimation.

tf.questionText: One advantage of a photograph is that it gives a clear visual record of how an area actually looks.
tf.explanation: Photographs capture the real appearance of an area, which is a key advantage.

tf.questionText: Haze and poor visibility can make features in the background of a photograph difficult to interpret.
tf.explanation: Distant background features may be faint or hidden by haze, lowering interpretation accuracy.

summary.correctAnswer: Ground (horizontal), oblique aerial and vertical aerial photographs.
summary.explanation: These differ by the position and angle of the camera when the photo is taken.

summary.correctAnswer: A photograph taken from ground level at eye height.
summary.explanation: It shows features side-on, as a person would normally see them.

summary.correctAnswer: A photograph taken from the air with the camera pointing straight down.
summary.explanation: It gives a plan view of the ground, similar to a map.

summary.correctAnswer: A photograph taken from the air with the camera tilted at an angle.
summary.explanation: It shows both the tops and sides of features.
They are arranged from nearest to farthest from the camera.

summary.correctAnswer: The area nearest the camera with the largest, clearest details.
summary.explanation: Objects here are easiest to identify because they appear big and sharp.

summary.correctAnswer: The most distant area, often showing the horizon.
summary.explanation: Features here appear small and may be faint or hazy.

summary.correctAnswer: Physical features are natural; human features are made by people.
summary.explanation: Rivers and hills are physical; roads and houses are human features.

summary.correctAnswer: They give a clear visual record of an area for study.
summary.explanation: They help in planning, research and recording the appearance of places.

summary.questionText: A limitation of photographs compared with maps
summary.correctAnswer: They usually lack a scale, key and place names.
summary.explanation: This makes accurate measurement and naming of features difficult.

hoq.questionText: A geographer must measure the exact distance between two villages and label them by name. Why is a topographical map more suitable than a ground photograph for this task?

options.text: The map provides a scale, a grid and names for accurate measurement and identification
The photograph can be folded more easily

hoq.explanation: Maps use a fixed scale, grid references and named features, enabling accurate distance measurement and identification that photographs cannot provide.

hoq.questionText: On a vertical aerial photograph, two areas have very different tones: one is dark and smooth-textured while the other is light with a regular grid pattern. What is the MOST reasonable interpretation?

options.text: Both areas are the same forest
The dark smooth area is likely a water body and the light gridded area is likely a built-up or cultivated area
The light gridded area is a lake

hoq.explanation: Tone, texture and pattern are interpretation clues: dark smooth tones often indicate water, while regular grid patterns suggest human planning such as fields or settlements.

hoq.questionText: Why can estimating the size of a feature in the background of a ground photograph give a misleading result if no reference object is used?

options.text: Background features are always coloured differently
Distance makes far features appear much smaller than they really are, so they may be underestimated
Background features are printed at a fixed scale
Background features are always larger than they appear

hoq.explanation: Because objects shrink in apparent size with distance, a distant feature looks small and may be wrongly judged unless compared with an object of known size.
